note: Every rule has a source with a short quote from the document, or source = null and needsReview = true. Nothing here is a prescription. A flight surgeon must review everything marked needsReview before real use.

rules.label: Normal week
rules.text: 6-7 sessions a week: about 30 minutes of aerobic exercise (interval or steady) plus 30-60 minutes of resistance exercise.

source.name: NASA OCHMO-TB-031 Exercise Overview
source.quote: Metabolic: Approximately 30 minutes of interval or steady-state exercise. Resistive/Strength: 30-60 minutes load-bearing training. (ISS long duration: 6-7 days/week, 30 minutes/session)

rules.label: Maximum heart rate
rules.text: Estimated as 220 minus age. A simple estimate only.

source.name: NASA OCHMO-TB-031 Exercise Overview
source.note: The document says "age-predicted maximum HR" but does not give a formula. 220 - age is a common estimate that this project chose.

rules.label: Minimum dose
rules.text: At least 3 sessions a week, each longer than 20 minutes, above 70% of maximum heart rate. Shown yellow if below.

source.name: NASA OCHMO-TB-031 Exercise Overview
source.quote: exercised three or more times per week during flight, at a HR >70% of their age-predicted maximum HR and for more than 20 minutes per session

rules.label: Protect aerobic capacity
rules.text: Keep aerobic capacity at 80% of baseline or higher.

source.name: NASA OCHMO-TB-031 Exercise Overview (NASA-STD-3001 Vol. 1 [V1 4003])
source.quote: The in-mission aerobic capacity shall be maintained ... at or above 80% of the pre-mission capacity

rules.label: Protect muscle strength
rules.text: Keep muscle strength at 80% of baseline or higher.

source.name: NASA OCHMO-TB-031 Exercise Overview (NASA-STD-3001 Vol. 1 [V1 4024])
source.quote: Countermeasures shall maintain in-mission skeletal muscle strength at or above 80% of baseline values.

rules.label: Protect bone
rules.text: Keep bone mineral density at 95% of baseline or higher (hip and spine). This device cannot measure it.

source.name: NASA OCHMO-TB-031 Exercise Overview (NASA-STD-3001 Vol. 1 [V1 4027])
source.quote: maintain bone mineral density (BMD) of the hip and spine at or above 95% of pre-mission values and at or above 90% for the femoral neck

rules.label: High-risk flag
rules.text: A drop of 20% or more in any tracked endpoint is a high-risk flag.

source.name: NASA OCHMO-TB-031 Exercise Overview
source.quote: 20% or greater aerobic reduction is associated with significant performance decrements ... the -20% requirement

rules.label: What protects bone and strength
rules.text: Resistance and treadmill volume are the main drivers for bone and strength.

source.name: NASA OCHMO-TB-031 Exercise Overview
source.quote: Resistance and treadmill volume loads were the key countermeasure factors associated with improved strength, bone, body composition, and cardiorespiratory endpoints.

rules.label: Never drop volume to zero
rules.text: Never drop resistance or treadmill volume to zero. On recovery days reduce the intensity, not the volume to nothing.

source.name: NASA OCHMO-TB-031 Exercise Overview
source.note: Follows from the rule above (volume is the main driver). The document does not state this policy in these words.

rules.label: Recovery-day intensity
rules.text: On recovery days keep intensity under 70% of maximum heart rate.

rules.label: Early trend rule
rules.text: A fall of 10% over 3 days is an early warning. Not applied by the app yet.

rules.label: Safety-gate wording
rules.text: Talk to the flight surgeon before changing your plan.

rules.label: Baseline for the proxy
rules.text: Baseline = the weekly average of the first 14 days of logged training. The proxy is minutes and logged lifts, not a VO2 or strength test.
